newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Former Argentine minister faces slander trial Dec 18.
newsitem.headline: Former Argentine minister faces slander trial Dec 18.

text.p: Former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo, who has named high-ranking officials in a crusade against graft, will stand trial later this month for slandering a High Court judge, a judge said on Saturday.
Cavallo, widely praised for beating hyperinflation and fostering growth while he was a minister, faces a maximum sentence of three years in jail if found guilty.
Federal Judge Adolfo Bagnasco set the public hearing for Dec. 18. A local news agency earlier reported that it was slated for Dec. 11.
Bagnasco told reporters that Cavallo "neither recognised that he caused offence nor showed signs of repentance, but simply generically retired what he said following supposed court guidelines."

The case dates back to 1993, when Cavallo called Supreme Court judges Augusto Belluscio and Enrique Petracchi "thieves and corrupt" for their ruling in a case against the Central Bank. Both sued, but Petracchi accepted a retraction last month.

Judge Bagnasco said the case was of vital importance for the credibility of the Argentine legal system, given the senior positions of Belluscio and Cavallo, who was sacked by President Carlos Menem in July.
"If a member of the court had conducted himself as Domingo Cavallo says, the whole of the judicial power would be discredited," said Bagnasco.
Cavallo twice tried to retract his statements but failed to convince Bagnasco or Belluscio that he was really sorry for what he said.

The former minister has whipped up a political storm since his sacking by accusing two senior ministers and Menem's top aide of covering up corruption. They deny the allegations and at least one plans to sue him.
